    rate per system volume. SMB C [g C/cm3 V]: Fast pool SMB carbon per sys-
    tem volume. ORG C [g C/cm3 V]: Stationary carbon per system volume.

sections.name: bound release
sections.desc:
Release of chemicals bound to colloids from surface soil.
     This follows the generation of colloids on the surface. The colloid generation
model should already have calculated the amount of released colloids as either a
fraction of the readily available colloids (Jarvis99), or as a fraction of the total
amount of soil in the mixing layer (Styczen88, Morgan98). The same fraction of the
immobile chemical on the surface is released in the colloid bound form.
     This reaction must be listed after the colloid generation reaction in the setup
file.

Chemical bound to colloids. If unspecified, the colloid bound form will not be
     traced.

attrs.doc: Immobile (or mixed form) chemical in the soil surface.

attrs.name: release
attrs.doc: Release rate of immobile chemical as colloids.

sections.name: denitrification
sections.desc:
Denitrification in soil, (conversion of nitrate to atmospheric nitrogen).
   In this model, it is made proportional to the CO2 development, as specified
by the parameter alpha, with a maximum rate specified by the parameter ’K’.
The denitrification is also affected by temperature and water pressure. Additional
denitrification from CO2 produced from fast OM pools can be triggered by setting
alpha fast or water factor fast different. This additional denitrification is limited
by K fast.
sections.sig:
< denitrification       (denprod denprod )                            ; Default Parton1996 value.
                         (alpha 0.1 [(g NO3-N/h)/(g CO2-C/h)])
                         (K 0.020833 [h−1 ])
                         (K fast K fast )
                         (alpha fast alpha fast )
                         (heat factor heat factor )
                         (water factor water factor )                  ; Has default value.
                         (water factor fast water factor fast )
                         (redox height redox height ) >

attrs.name: denprod
attrs.doc: Denitrification products.

attrs.name: alpha
attrs.doc: Anaerobic denitrification constant for slow pools.

attrs.name: K
attrs.doc: Maximum fraction of nitrate converted at each time step from slow pools.

attrs.name: K fast
attrs.doc:
Maximum fraction of nitrate converted at each time step from fast pools. By
    default this is identical to ’K’.

attrs.name: alpha fast
attrs.doc:
Anaerobic denitrification constant for fast pools. This applies to the CO2
    produced from turnover of fast OM pools. By default, this is identical to
    alpha.

attrs.name: heat factor
attrs.doc: Heat factor. By default, use a build in function valid for temperate climates.

attrs.name: water factor
attrs.kind: Optional parameter (has default value with 2 points)
attrs.doc:
(water_factor (0.7 [] 0 []) (1 [] 1 []))
        Parameter description:
        Water potential factor for slow pools. This is a function of the current water
        content as a fraction of the maximal water content.

attrs.name: water factor fast
attrs.doc:
Water potential factor for fast pools By default, this is identical to the ’wa-
        ter factor’ parameter.

attrs.name: redox height
attrs.doc:
Height (a negative number) blow which redox processes start. All NO3 below
        this height will be denitrified immediately. By default no redox denitrification
        occurs.

attrs.name: converted
attrs.doc: Amount of denitrification.

attrs.name: converted fast
attrs.doc: Additional denitrification due to turnover in fast pools.

attrs.name: converted redox
attrs.doc: Additional denitrification due to chemical redox processes.

attrs.name: potential
attrs.doc: Potential amount of denitrification at anarobic conditions.

attrs.name: potential fast
attrs.doc: Additional potential due to turnover in fast pools.

   Used by chemistry N reaction (see 24.3, page 145) .

 < denitrification       (denprod denprod )                            ; Default Parton1996 value.
                         (alpha 0.1 [(g NO3-N/h)/(g CO2-C/h)])
                         (K 0.020833 [h−1 ])
                         (K fast K fast )
                         (alpha fast alpha fast )
                         (heat factor heat factor )
                         (water factor water factor )                  ; Has default value.
                         (water factor fast water factor fast )
                         (redox height redox height ) >
   denprod : denprod component (see chapter 32)
    Component (default ‘Parton1996’)
    Denitrification products.
   alpha: number [(g NO3-N/h)/(g CO2-C/h)]
    Parameter (default 0.1)
    Anaerobic denitrification constant for slow pools.
   K : number [h−1 ]
    Parameter (default 0.020833)
    Maximum fraction of nitrate converted at each time step from slow pools.
   K fast: number [h−1 ]
    Optional parameter
    Maximum fraction of nitrate converted at each time step from fast pools. By
    default this is identical to ’K’.
   alpha fast: number [(g NO3-N/h)/(g CO2-C/h)]
    Optional parameter
    Anaerobic denitrification constant for fast pools. This applies to the CO2
    produced from turnover of fast OM pools. By default, this is identical to
    alpha.
   heat factor : plf [dg C → <none>]
    Optional parameter
    Heat factor. By default, use a build in function valid for temperate climates.
   water factor : plf [<fraction> → <none>]
    Optional parameter (has default value with 2 points)

        (water_factor (0.7 [] 0 []) (1 [] 1 []))

        Parameter description:
        Water potential factor for slow pools. This is a function of the current water
        content as a fraction of the maximal water content.

       water factor fast: plf [<fraction> → <none>]
        Optional parameter
        Water potential factor for fast pools By default, this is identical to the ’wa-
        ter factor’ parameter.

       redox height: number [cm]
        Optional parameter
        Height (a negative number) blow which redox processes start. All NO3 below
        this height will be denitrified immediately. By default no redox denitrification
        occurs.

Log Variables
       converted : number [g/cm3 /h] sequence
        Amount of denitrification.

       converted fast: number [g/cm3 /h] soil cells
        Additional denitrification due to turnover in fast pools.

       converted redox : number [g/cm3 /h] soil cells
        Additional denitrification due to chemical redox processes.

       potential : number [g/cm3 /h] soil cells
        Potential amount of denitrification at anarobic conditions.

       potential fast: number [g/cm3 /h] soil cells
        Additional potential due to turnover in fast pools.

attrs.name: equilibrium
attrs.doc: Function for calculating equilibrium between A and B.

attrs.name: secondary
attrs.doc:
Equilibrium should happen in the secondary domain. There will only be a
        reaction when there is water in the secondary domain (inter-aggregate pores),
        at both the beginning and end of the timestep. By default, only the content of
        the primary domain (soil-bound and intra-aggregate pores), will be included
     in the reaction. There is no way to use this model to specify an equilibrium
     reaction in the tertiary domain (biopores).

attrs.name: surface
attrs.doc: Equilibrium should happen in the surface.

attrs.name: A
attrs.doc: Name of first soil component in equilibrium.

attrs.name: B
attrs.doc: Name of second soil component in equilibrium.

attrs.name: k AB
attrs.doc: Tranformation rate from soil component ’A’ to ’B’.

attrs.name: k BA
attrs.doc:
Tranformation rate from soil component ’B’ to ’A’. By default, this is identical
     to ’k AB’.

attrs.name: colloid
attrs.doc:
Let ’rho b’ denote content of specified chemical. This might affect the evalu-
     ation of the ’k AB’ and ’k BA’ parameter expressions, as well as the ’equilib-
     rium’ model. By default, ’rho b’ will be the soil dry bulk density.

attrs.name: primary
attrs.doc:
Equilibrium should happen in the primary domain. If true, the content of the
     primary soil domain (soil-bound and intra-aggregate pores), will be included
     in the reaction. By default, this will be true if ’secondary’ is false, and be
     false if ’secondary’ is true.

attrs.name: S AB
attrs.doc: Converted from A to B in soil this timestep (may be negative).

attrs.name: surface AB
attrs.doc: Converted from A to B on surface this timestep (may be negative).

sections.name: sorption
sections.desc:
Kinetic linear sorption equilibrium. Faster than the ’equilibrium’ reaction model,
more flexible than the ’adsorption’ reaction model.
sections.sig:
< sorption (solute solute )
                  (K clay K clay )
                  (K OC K OC )
                  (K d K d )
                  (sorbed sorbed )
                  (colloid colloid )
                  (k sorption k sorption )
                  (k desorption k desorption )
                  (soil enrichment factor 1 []) >

attrs.name: solute
attrs.doc:
Name of solute form of chemical. If this chemical has equilibrium sorption,
        only the colute part is used.

attrs.name: K clay
attrs.doc:
Clay dependent distribution parameter. It is multiplied with the soil clay
        fraction to get the clay part of the ’K d’ factor. If ’K OC’ is specified, ’K clay’
        defaults to 0.

attrs.name: K OC
attrs.doc:
Humus dependent distribution parameter. It is multiplied with the soil organic
        carbon fraction to get the carbon part of the ’K d’ factor. By default, ’K OC’
        is equal to ’K clay’.

attrs.name: K d
attrs.doc:
Equillibrium parameter: M = C (K d rho b + Theta) Here M is the total
        amount, C is solute concentration, K d is this parameter, rho b is the dry
        bulk density, and Theta is the volumetric water content. By default, K d is
        calculated from K clay and K OC.

attrs.name: sorbed
attrs.doc: Name of sorbed form of chemical.

attrs.name: colloid
attrs.doc: Sorp to this chemical instead of to the soil matrix.

attrs.name: k sorption
attrs.doc: Sorption rate.

attrs.name: k desorption
attrs.doc: Desorption rate. By default, this is identical to ’k sorption’.

attrs.name: soil enrichment factor
attrs.doc:
Multiply K d with this number if ’colloid’ is set. This represents how much
        more accesible colloids is compared to the soil matrix.

attrs.doc: Sorption on surface this timestep (may be negative).
